subject: koala
pitch: A sleepy koala hugging a eucalyptus branch. Soft ash-grey fur with a cream chest and cream-lined fluffy ears, a big black leathery nose, half-closed drowsy brown eyes, strong grey paws with dark claws, and a sprig of blue-green eucalyptus leaves in one hand, mid-munch.
reasoning:
I'm planning a koala model built with TypeScript using the SDK, sized at roughly 0.7 meters sitting height, constructed from simplified geometric primitives like spheres for the body shape rather than complex lofts.

I'm sketching the skeleton: hip and chest joints forming a spine, a head joint with ear joints attached, and arm chains running from shoulders through elbows to paws. The koala's arms curve forward to wrap around a diagonal branch positioned at chest height.

For the chain structure, each limb uses a three-point polyline (shoulder/elbow/wrist or hip/knee/foot) producing two joint spans plus a tip joint, with camelCase names like upperArmL and forearmL. Legs follow the same pattern bent forward for a sitting pose, and I'm deciding to keep the tail minimal or skip it entirely.

For the body, I'm shaping a mottled gray sphere for the torso with a flattened cream chest patch in front, then a large round head with small flattened ears that have cream inner patches, positioning everything using world coordinates for the parts.

The face gets a leathery black nose, half-closed dark brown eyes with fur-colored lid caps to give that drowsy koala look, and I'm placing leaves near the mouth for the munching pose. For the branch, I'm sweeping a tapered curved path through a few points with a brown bark color so it reads as a tree limb the koala grips with its paws.

Now I'm working out the arm and paw geometry so both paws land naturally on the branch's curve — one paw gripping the branch for support while the other holds the eucalyptus sprig up near the mouth for that mid-munch moment.

Then I'm figuring out how to build the leaves themselves: using extruded lanceolate outlines for each sickle-shaped leaf, colored in a muted blue-green, strung along a swept stem that curves from the paw outward and upward.

Defining leaf outline points...

Now I'm sketching the stem path and leaf placement positions, planning roughly seven leaves attached at points along a curved stem with small thickness.

I'm placing each leaf individually with its own base position and direction vector, alternating between two blue-green fur colors, then moving on to building short sitting legs for the koala using a joint chain with tapered sweep radii.

For paws, I'm adding dark grey spheres with small cone-shaped claws at each foot, mirroring positions for the right leg. I'm also sizing the pear-shaped body sphere and sketching fluffy outer and cream inner ear spheres attached to the head bone.

Now I'm placing the head sphere relative to its joint, then positioning the nose, cream muzzle patch, brown eyes with drowsy lid covers, and skipping a defined mouth for simplicity. I'm setting up the joint hierarchy starting with hips as root, then chest and head as children, and beginning to work out the arm chain parentage.

Defining fur paints and branch sweep...

I'm checking that the lowest points of the model sit near ground level — feet, legs, and the branch all need to clear or touch y=0 without floating or sinking too far. I realize the body sphere's current radius makes it float above the ground, so I'm lowering its center to around 0.24 and recalculating the hip, chest, and head positions to keep proportions consistent while bringing the bottom close to the floor.

Now I'm working out the arm joint chains for both sides, positioning shoulders, elbows, and paws so the koala appears to grip the branch near its mouth, and checking that the branch radius stays nested inside the paw spheres at the contact points.

I'm sketching the sprig leaves held near the paw, running a tapered stem sweep from the paw position upward with a shrinking radius function and a muted green color, making sure the stem path stays near the cheek without colliding with the chest or muzzle geometry.

Now I'm placing individual leaves along the stem at successive points, giving each one its own outward-pointing direction vector, and working through which perpendicular axis to use for leaf width so they orient naturally rather than collapsing into degenerate directions.

I'll set leaf thickness, length, and alternating green colors for variation, then decide to attach leaves and stem sweeps to the paw joint on the left arm chain so they move naturally with the limb.

Now I'm mapping out the full koala body: naming leg and arm chains, setting up tapered sweep radii for limbs, and positioning paws and feet so their undersides sit flush with the ground. I'm defining claw placement, ear structure with cream inner sections, chest and muzzle details, eye and eyelid geometry for a sleepy look, and nose coloring, working through the coordinate math to keep everything proportioned against the head and body spheres.

Writing part construction code...
